page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-16xCPU-96GB is a virtual server instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz on a KVM hypervisor. The instance provisions 16 x86_64 vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores with a shared allocation model, paired with 96.0 GB of system memory to achieve a density of 6.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not bundle local disk storage, dedicated GPU hardware, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on attached external storage and network provisioning.

Benchmark evaluations indicate steady multi-threaded capacity alongside lower single-thread throughput. Single-core execution in stress-ng registers at 779.18 in the bottom 10 percent of recorded results, reflecting the 2.0 GHz clock rate. Multi-core performance reaches middle-tier levels with a stress-ng score of 12409.56 and a Geekbench multi-core result of 13359.0, supplemented by strong text processing metrics at 2638.0. Memory bandwidth delivers 48.36 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 28.85 GB/sec for writes.

With 6.0 GB of RAM per core, the hardware configuration provides substantial memory capacity relative to compute allocations without the expense of dedicated CPU pins. The primary technical tradeoff involves shared core tenancy and the absence of high-speed local disk storage, which limits suitability for latency-critical, single-threaded processing. The architecture aligns with horizontally scaled microservices, Redis caching tiers, CI/CD runners, and batch ETL data processing.
